_comment: Release notes shown in the app ('What's new' pop-up after an update, and Settings > Release notes) and on the GitHub release page. Newest first. EVERY Android release needs an entry here whose version matches the release (1.0.<workflow run number>); the release workflow refuses to publish otherwise. Keep it high level and in plain English.

improved: Report a bug now sends your report straight to the project's bug list when you press Send — no GitHub account or browser needed.

new: Report a bug from inside the app (phone, desktop and web): describe the problem, see exactly what will be sent, and press Send — it goes straight to the project's bug list. No GitHub account needed.
improved: Long pop-up forms on the desktop/web app keep their buttons visible at the bottom.
“What's new” now shows everything new since the version you had before — including updates you skipped — not just the latest one.

fixed: Camera screens (VIN scan, QR code, photos): the Flashlight, Cancel and Done buttons were almost invisible on the dark camera panel. They're now white and clearly visible in light and dark mode.

new: Metrics: a new tab on every vehicle showing how its history adds up — records, total spent, how often each service was done and the miles/months between them, by category (chart), by service and by year.

Everything is tappable and filters everything else: a time range, maintenance or repairs, DIY or shop, a category, a service, a year (or just its repairs). Tap “Total spent” to see every record with a cost, most expensive first, adding up to the total. Tap a record to open it.
A record whose mileage is lower than the one before it (usually a typo) is flagged and left out of averages.

Specs that are parts now appear on the Parts tab automatically — engine oil type, oil filter and spark plug part numbers, tire sizes, battery group, wiper sizes, fluids and more. Change the spec and the part updates; clear it and the part goes away.
improved: Reminders: overdue ones are at the very top, then the ones coming up, then everything in good standing.
A vehicle's sections are now in the order you use them — Reminders, Parts, History, Specs — and it opens on Reminders. The separate Odometer section is gone (use the Mileage / Update mileage button).
The manufacturer's parts site is now only on the Parts tab (the duplicate button at the top was removed).

new: Shopping list: collect everything you need before doing the work. Add a reminder's supplies (“Add to shopping list” — with the OEM part number and oil type etc. you saved), add a saved part from the Parts tab, or type an item in. Each item can have a quantity, OEM part number, specification, notes, a vehicle and the reminder it's for.
Search any item at Amazon, Walmart or Advance Auto Parts, tick items off as you buy them, and remove what you don't need. The list syncs between your phone and computer.
Open it from the cart button on the Garage (phone) or “Shopping list” at the top (computer).
improved: Buying something never marks the maintenance as done and never adds an expense on its own — record the job in the history when you do it.
Tap a reminder to open it: “Mark as done” fills in today's date and your current mileage and adds the job to the history in one tap. “Edit schedule” changes how often it's due.
fixed: Marking a reminder done now clears “Overdue” right away — the last-done mileage is updated too, not just the date.
Adding a record of any kind (for example a tire rotation saved as a repair) now updates the matching reminder.

new: Smart Shopping (optional): “Find supplies” on maintenance reminders and a shop button on parts open a search at Amazon, Walmart or Advance Auto Parts — built from your vehicle's specs and part numbers (exact part numbers first). Turn it off or choose your retailers in Settings → Smart Shopping.
Connect to your computer by scanning a QR code — no address, username or password to type. On the computer: “Connect a phone (QR code)” in the desktop app, or Settings → Connect a phone.
Add vehicle: pick the make from a list, and the model for that make and year (from the U.S. NHTSA vehicle database). You can still type anything.
Add a photo of your vehicle (camera or gallery); it shows in your garage.
Settings → Report a bug: opens a pre-filled bug report you can review before sending.
improved: The Garage now shows just your vehicles. Open a vehicle to see what's coming up, with a smaller header and buttons so there's more room for your records.
Motorcycle parts and owner links fixed (Ducati, Kawasaki, Yamaha, KTM, Harley-Davidson and more).
A job with no cost entered shows $0.00 instead of a dash.
New car and motorcycle icons: a sedan and a sport bike (the old motorcycle looked like a bicycle).
fixed: Editing a vehicle and going to the barcode scanner (or camera) and back no longer loses what you typed or the VIN-decoded details.

improved: Every release now includes all downloads in one place: the Android app plus the desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux, all the same version.
fixed: The desktop app downloads were published separately and hard to find on the Releases page.

new: Settings → Sync: “Change address” (keeps you signed in — handy when your computer gets a new address after a restart) and “Sign in again”.
improved: When syncing fails, the Garage now says so clearly, explains why in plain English, and shows when the last good sync was.
Signing in to a different computer or server sends everything on this phone there, so both end up with the same records.
fixed: Sync could silently stop working (for example after the login ended) without telling you.

new: Two new types with their own icons: “Scheduled service” (e.g. the 30,000-mile service) and “Wheel repair / refinish”.
improved: History items imported from Carfax now show what was done (e.g. “Air filter replaced”) with the right icon, instead of “Custom / other”.

new: Connecting to your computer is easier: just type its address (like 192.168.1.20:8077) and the app asks before using plain HTTP on your home network.
improved: Clear, plain-English messages when connecting fails (wrong port, firewall, different Wi-Fi, wrong password), instead of technical errors.
The app checks that the address really is a Ratchet Wrench server before signing in, and ignores anything pasted after the port.
If the first sync after signing in hits a problem, you're still signed in and it retries automatically.
fixed: “Unable to parse TLS packet header” when connecting to the desktop app or Docker server.
One photo the server couldn't accept no longer stops the whole sync.

new: Release notes: after each update, a “What's new” message shows what changed the first time you open the app.
Settings now has a Release notes section listing what changed in every version.
The VIN scanner also reads the printed VIN, not just the barcode. You confirm a VIN read from text before it's used.
Flashlight button, zoom slider and tap-to-focus on the VIN scanner.
improved: Much better barcode reading: the scanner now looks at a far sharper picture (1080p instead of 640×480).

new: The camera shows small previews of the photos you've taken.
improved: Photos are saved without hidden location details on the phone's copy.
fixed: Photos no longer disappear when you turn the phone while using the camera or adding an entry.
Photos are no longer sideways or flipped — they're saved and shown the way you took them, even with auto-rotate off.

new: Settings button on the Garage screen, and an About section in Settings.
improved: Every release is now tested by automatically tapping through the app before it's published.
fixed: The app no longer crashes when opened with a vehicle saved, or when adding an entry (icons were missing).
Deleting an entry now always works.

improved: If the app ever closes unexpectedly, it offers to copy the error details next time (kept on your phone only).
fixed: Scan barcode no longer crashes the app.

new: The app updates itself: new versions download on Wi-Fi (or ask first on mobile data) and install after a quick confirmation.
